newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta records surplus, makes payment on net debt.
newsitem.headline: Alberta records surplus, makes payment on net debt.

text.p: The Canadian province of Alberta posted its third consecutive surplus in fiscal 1996-97 and made a C$2.5 billion payment on net debt, said Alberta's treasurer on Thursday.
"This is a good day for Albertans," said Treasurer Stockwell Day in releasing the province's financial and performance results.
"With this payment, we saved C$201 million in interest costs in 1996-97. Our fiscal plan is working, steadily bringing us from under yesterday's bills," Day said.
The payment reduced the province's net debt to C$3.7 billion, excluding pension obligations, Day said.
Previous surpluses of C$1.13 billion in 1995-96 and C$958 million in 1994-95 were used to pay down Alberta's net debt.
The unexpectedly high surplus was due mostly to strong resource and income tax revenues and a C$371 million windfall from the elimination of some existing pension obligations, Day said.
